title: Observability staging & export-path refactor: reduce allocations and decouple exporters
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Background: Our runtime observability path has accumulated ad-hoc exporters and sync I/O that inflates p50/p95 CPU usage and allocs under production loads. This ticket consolidates export wiring, upgrades the OpenTelemetry SDK to 1.14, and introduces a lightweight asynchronous span buffer + nonblocking exporter adapter. Goals: (1) Reduce per-request allocation in the hot path by 40% for typical inference requests, (2) Eliminate blocking disk/HTTP calls from the main request loop, (3) Provide a backward-compatible exporter shim so teams can migrate off custom exporters incrementally, (4) Add observability for the observability pipeline (health metrics, backpressure hotspots, and queue depth). Out of scope: replacing vendor-specific long-term storage, changing sampling policies platform-wide (this ticket only exposes hooks).
comments: 2026-02-10 - Ravi Patel: Triage notes — traced several p95 spikes to exporter flushes and JSON encoder allocations. Proposed approach: upgrade OTEL, add async ring buffer for spans, and introduce an exporter proxy that accepts both old and new exporter configs.

2026-02-15 - Mariana Lopez: Design review completed with infra and runtime teams. Decided to keep existing config surface for customers; add an opt-in feature flag `observability.async_exporter` before turning on globally. Trade-offs: adding the buffer adds a small bounded heap usage but removes blocking syscalls from request threads.
2026-02-22 - Implementation: Introduced local ring-buffer (cap 10k spans) with backpressure metrics. Initial microbench shows 37% reduction in allocs for small-span workloads (see PR).

2026-03-01 - Code review (ENG): Reviewers suggested tightening visibility for exporter proxy and adding strict error handling so exporter failures don't drop traces silently. Added a 10s retry with exponential backoff and circuit-breaker metric.

2026-03-05 - QA: Canary in staging ran for 72h against the conversational benchmark set. Observed stable CPU and tail-latency reduction: p95 down ~12%, p99 down ~6% for the serving runtime. Notable: increased queued spans during a 3m burst (queue peaked at 82% capacity) — added metric and alert (telemetry.observability.buffer_usage > 80%).

2026-03-10 - Security: Requested a short assessment of exporter TLS configs. Confirmed we will preserve existing TLS settings and do not introduce any new plaintext fallback. Security review scheduled for 2026-03-14.

2026-03-12 - Mariana Lopez: Preparing rollout plan: weekly staged enablement by customer cohort; initial subset: internal-dev, staging, then 10% of production traffic with fallback to legacy exporter if buffer saturation sustained >2m.
